Scientific research has confirmed what cat owners have long suspected: a cat's meow functions as a direct command aimed specifically at humans. In a study conducted in Brazil, researchers led by Naila Fukimoto at the University of São Paulo evaluated 38 domestic cats that were known by their owners to be particularly vocal around mealtime.

During the experiment, each cat's favorite treat was placed inside a small plastic container perforated with holes, allowing the animals to see and smell the food without being able to reach it themselves. The researchers then observed each cat for one minute with an attentive person present in the room, and for one minute while completely alone. 

When a human caregiver was present, the cats produced a combined total of 86 meows, compared to just 20 meows when left by themselves. Furthermore, many of the cats repeatedly shifted their gaze back and forth between the person and the sealed container, effectively pointing out the obstacle. When left alone in the room, the felines largely remained motionless and stared quietly toward the exit door. 

Published in the journal Animal Behaviour, these findings reinforce long-standing behavioral observations. Because adult cats rarely meow at one another and feral felines vocalize far less frequently than house pets, animal behaviorists have theorized that meowing evolved primarily as a tool for interacting with humans. This study provides strong evidence that the meow serves as a recipient-specific signal directed toward the human capable of resolving a problem.

However, the authors note that the trial examined a relatively small sample of cats already inclined to vocalize around food and tested only a single scenario, meaning not every meow represents a demand. Even so, the results pave the way for future investigations into whether cats modify the acoustic structure of their meows to communicate distinct requests.

[Fukimoto, N., Albuquerque, N., & Savalli, C. (2026). Domestic cats (Felis catus) direct meows at humans during an unsolvable task. Animal Behaviour. DOI: 10.1016/j.anbehav.2026.123756]

Selila’s clinic sign was being polished to a shine by a talking octopus. The beautiful doctor had just finished her coffee when she looked up to see a unicorn knocking at the door with its hoof.

"Emergency?" Selila asked, putting on her stethoscope.

The unicorn nodded and pulled a trembling little creature from its rainbow-colored mane—a mouse wearing a suit and gold-rimmed glasses. It clutched a miniature briefcase, its face pale blue.

"Did you swallow another talking candy again?" Selila sighed.

The mouse nodded weakly. "I am the president of the Financial District Mouse Bank. This morning, a client gave me a 'Honesty Candy.' After swallowing it, I started telling the truth..."

The unicorn added, "He told all his clients, 'Your deposits have actually been lost by me buying stocks.' Now, mice all over the city are chasing him."

Selila skillfully opened her magical medicine cabinet and took out a bottle labeled "Forgetfulness Cough Syrup." "Open wide."

After drinking it, the mouse burped, and his glasses fell off. "What did I just say?"

"Nothing," Selila smiled. "You just dreamed that you became a model of integrity."

Suddenly, a phoenix dove down outside the window, its wings tangled in fan ribbons. "Dr. Selila! I'm being chased by fans again!" the phoenix wailed. "They're plucking my feathers for lucky charms. If this continues, I'll go bald!"

Selila pulled out a feather comb. "Turn around. Let me give you a fireproof hairstyle that guarantees no one will recognize you."

Ten minutes later, the phoenix flew away with a head full of frizzy curls, satisfied. "This style is so tacky; the fans definitely won't recognize me!"

Before leaving, the unicorn traced a rainbow on the desk with the tip of its horn: "I’ve paid for the medical fees."

Selila finally breathed a sigh of relief, but then she heard a roar coming from the basement. She rushed downstairs and saw a dragon stuck in the pet door, its belly round and swollen.

"Eating the neighbor's automatic feeder again?" Selila put her hands on her hips.

Selila took out a magnifying glass and chanted a spell against the dragon's belly. Suddenly, the feeder dinged and ejected dog food. The dragon let out a loud belch, shaking the entire clinic three times.

"If you eat tech products again, I’m ordering you a vegetarian meal plan," Selila said.

The dragon teared up. "You’re so cruel!"

Just then, the phone rang. A panicked voice came from the other end: "Dr. Selila! My cat swallowed the neighbor’s portal key again. Now it’s appearing in the kitchen and on the ceiling simultaneously!"

Selila picked up her magic stethoscope and said to the dragon, "See? At least you know where you are."

She smiled and walked toward the door. From the pocket of her white coat, the head of the mouse bank president popped out, whispering, "Doctor, do you think... should I tell the truth to my clients?"

Selila looked down at it. "You just took 'Forgetfulness Cough Syrup,' not 'Honesty Candy.'"

The mouse paused, adjusted his glasses, and asked, "Then my deposits..."

"They're safe," Selila winked. "I swapped them for some 'Security Mint Candies' for you."

Rainbows shimmered outside the window, and strange animal noises echoed throughout the clinic. Selila opened her medical record book and wrote: "Patient #1887 – President of the Mouse Bank. Diagnosis: Excessive Anxiety. Prescription: Kind little lies."

Sunlight streamed through the magical glass windows, illuminating the name tag on her white coat. Below it was a small inscription: "All creatures deserve to be treated gently, even if they occasionally eat their neighbors' homes."
